text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A Vilnius court began proceedings against former prime minister Adolfas Slezevicius. He is suspected of abusing his public position for private benefit.

- The election comission applies double standards to Lithuanian exiles. Three were elected to parliament last autumn but U.S. enviromental protection expert Valdas Adamkus has been excluded from next month's local election list on the grounds he has dual citizenship.
- There were 3.71 million inhabitants in Lithuania at the begining of 1997 but the birth rate was the lowest since 1945.

- Greek President Constantinos Stephanopoulos told his Lithuanian counterpart Algirdas Brazauskas that his country supports Lithuania's desire to become a member of the European Union and NATO. Brazauskas is in Greece on a three-day visit.
- The Polish parliament approved the suggestion of Vytautas Landsbergis, the chairman of Lithuania's parliament, to start a bilateral parliamentary institution.
- A three-day conference began in Vilnius to examine how foreign investors can participate in the reconstruction of Vilnius' Old Town.
- The government plans to take action against municipalities and other publicly funded institutions that do not pay their energy bills.
- The import of deboned and ground poultry products from EU countries will be banned from March 1 on the grounds that they pose a health hazard.
